title: Fertility-Sparing Surgery in Cervical Cancer (Trachelectomy): Patient Selection, SHAPE Trial and Obstetric Outcomes
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: Berek & Hacker's Gynecologic Oncology 7th Edition Ch 10
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Cervical Cancer (Version 1.2024)
Plante M et al. Simple Hysterectomy or Conization in Low-Risk Early-Stage Cervical Cancer (SHAPE). NEJM 2024

steps.say: Radical trachelectomy is an established surgical technique that allows young women with early-stage invasive cervical carcinoma to preserve reproductive potential without compromising long-term oncological survival.
steps.tx: In young women desiring **fertility sparing**, **radical trachelectomy**, whether performed via **vaginal trachelectomy (Dargent)** or abdominal approach, achieves **uterine corpus preservation** by resecting the cervix, upper 1 to 2 cm of vagina, and medial parametrium while conserving the corpus, fundus, and ovaries.

steps.say: Candidate selection for radical trachelectomy requires rigorous pre-operative clinical and radiological evaluation to ensure the primary tumor is strictly confined to the ectocervix.
steps.tx: Strict oncological **eligibility criteria** mandate Stage IA1 with LVSI, Stage IA2, or Stage IB1 lesions, **tumor diameter <=2 cm**, squamous or typical HPV-associated adenocarcinoma histology, unequivocal **absence of upper canal involvement**, and radiologically or pathologically confirmed **negative nodes** without extrauterine disease spread.

rows: Stage IB2, IB3, IIA or higher
Squamous cell or typical HPV adenocarcinoma
Free canal >= 8-10 mm to internal os
Involvement of upper third or internal os

steps.say: Certain histopathological variants exhibit high propensities for early haematogenous dissemination and occult nodal metastases, rendering conservative fertility preservation inappropriate.
steps.tx: Major oncological surgical **contraindications** include aggressive tumor biologies such as small cell **neuroendocrine carcinoma**, **gastric-type adenocarcinoma**, adenoma malignum, deep cervical stromal invasion, pelvic nodal metastases, and **tumor >2 cm** in diameter, all of which mandate standard radical hysterectomy or primary chemoradiotherapy.

left.title: Permitted Favorable Histologies
points: Minimal stromal invasion with low risk of occult metastasis

right.title: Absolute Contraindications
points: Small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and large cell neuroendocrine
Presence of lymph node metastasis or tumor > 2 cm

steps.say: The most critical intraoperative milestone during radical trachelectomy is histopathological confirmation that the superior surgical margin is completely clear of malignancy.
steps.tx: Intraoperative **frozen section endocervical margin** assessment is mandatory before proceeding to uterine reconstruction. Surgeons must confirm **internal os clearance** with a histological tumor-free **8 to 10 mm margin**; any positive margin on frozen section necessitates immediate conversion to complete radical hysterectomy.

nodes.label: Perform pelvic lymph node dissection to exclude occult nodal spread
Transect cervix 5 mm below internal os and amputate specimen
Send upper endocervical ring for rapid intraoperative frozen section
Confirm minimum 8 to 10 mm margin clear before performing uterovaginal anastomosis

steps.say: The landmark prospective SHAPE randomized trial published in 2024 has reshaped surgical management in women with low-risk early-stage cervical cancer.
steps.tx: The prospective randomized **SHAPE trial** by **Plante 2024** demonstrated that **simple hysterectomy/conization** is oncologically non-inferior to radical hysterectomy in **low-risk cervical cancer** (tumors <=2 cm with <50% stromal invasion and negative nodes), demonstrating a 3-year pelvic recurrence rate below 3% with substantially reduced surgical morbidity.

left.title: SHAPE Trial: Conservative Arm
points: Simple hysterectomy or cone biopsy with lymph node staging
Significantly lower intraoperative urinary and bladder complications

right.title: SHAPE Trial: Radical Arm
points: Type B/C radical hysterectomy with parametrial resection
Higher rate of long-term bladder dysfunction and lymphedema

steps.say: Because excision of the cervix removes the mechanical barrier supporting the pregnant uterus, placing a permanent cervical cerclage is an integral step of the trachelectomy procedure.
steps.tx: Placement of an intraoperative **prophylactic cerclage** using non-absorbable braided **Mersilene tape** or polypropylene suture is performed at the level of the anatomical internal os. This **isthmic cerclage** provides mechanical reinforcement for **cervical incompetence prevention**, significantly reducing mid-trimester spontaneous pregnancy loss in future gestations.

nodes.label: Complete radical resection of cervix and upper vaginal cuff
Pass Mersilene polyester tape circumferentially around uterine isthmus
Secure knot anteriorly or posteriorly to avoid erosion into bladder
Anastomose lower uterine segment to vaginal cuff with absorbable sutures

steps.say: Pregnancies conceived after radical trachelectomy are categorized as high-risk and require specialized maternal-fetal surveillance throughout gestation.
steps.tx: Following radical trachelectomy, all viable pregnancies mandate delivery via planned **elective cesarean delivery** at **37-38 weeks** gestation. Vaginal delivery is strictly contraindicated due to cervical absence and the presence of the permanent stitch; careful **cerclage preservation** during hysterotomy enables future pregnancies.

left.title: Obstetric Management Rules
points: High-risk maternal-fetal medicine surveillance throughout gestation
Serial transvaginal ultrasound monitoring of isthmic residual length
Mandatory planned elective cesarean section at 37 to 38 weeks

right.title: Prohibited Interventions
points: Trial of labor and vaginal delivery are strictly prohibited
Avoid routine removal of Mersilene cerclage band during cesarean
Low-transverse uterine incision placed above cerclage site

steps.say: Long-term data from international registries indicate that radical trachelectomy offers oncological outcomes indistinguishable from standard radical hysterectomy in carefully selected patients.
steps.tx: Large international cohorts demonstrate definitive **oncological equivalence** between radical trachelectomy and radical hysterectomy in tumors <=2 cm, reporting an exceptional local **recurrence rate 3-5%** and excellent reproductive success with a cumulative **live birth rate >65-70%** among women attempting conception. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.
